data.exact_reserve_text: In 2017, there has been an overall deficit of GBP 1.8m on prior year reserves (2016:surplus GBP 0.7m). This has been primarily generated by the reduction in premium on casualty reinsurance class of business.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Commutation removed a significant amount of reserve risk and was completed at a profit, reducing reserve risk on the affected years.

named_events.loss_description: Part of the 2017 HIM series; aggregate estimated net exposure to HIM events was $10.4m (8% of Stamp) with 85% impacting 2017 and 15% impacting 2016.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2017 were GBP 54.925m. Using the gross claims development table, prior-year (<=2015) re-estimation produced a small net adverse movement of approximately GBP 0.44m (about 0.8% of opening reserves), i.e. a modest strengthening. The Managing Agent however reports an overall prior-year deficit of GBP 1.8m (reported narrative appears to be net of reinsurance) primarily driven by a reduction in premium on the casualty reinsurance class. The syndicate continues to cite US casualty commutation activity removing reserve risk and 2017 natural catastrophes (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria and Californian wildfires) as key loss drivers in the year, with the HIM events' net exposure quoted in USD.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (gross) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross cumulative estimates) and yields a small adverse movement (~GBP 0.44m). The Managing Agent narrative reports an overall prior-year deficit of GBP 1.8m which appears to be a NET figure (after reinsurance) - no explicit gross prior-year movement line was provided. Named-event exposures are quoted in USD in the narrative ($10.4m HIM); these were not converted to GBP and therefore net_loss_gbp_m fields are left null. The triangle and movement narrative cover slightly different scopes; reported gross PYD used here is the triangle-derived gross movement and is therefore the best available gross measure.
